keydlg.lead: This link {START_EMPHASISED_TEXT}is{CLOSE_EMPHASISED_TEXT} your account. Whoever holds it is you. There is no recovery — save it as a bookmark or in your password manager.

foot.baseline: The baseline is 12.5 % — pure guessing. Every figure here is a deviation from it.
check.charset: Letters, digits, spaces, hyphen, underscore only.
check.edges: Must not start or end with a space, - or _.
check.repeats: Not the same character four times over.
check.reserved: That name is reserved for the site itself.
check.vulgar: This name goes on a public leaderboard. Not this one.
gate.heading: What should we call you?
gate.lead: The name goes on the public leaderboard and beside every single session in the downloadable record. It is the only thing about you that is not anonymous — everything else runs under a random id.
gate.label: Display name
gate.hint: 3 to {INTERPOLATION} characters. Letters, digits, spaces, hyphen, underscore.
gate.note: A human approves the name before it is published. Until then public pages show a mask — to you we always show it. You can remove it at any time; the sessions then stand under the id, still verifiable.
refuse.shapeless: The name has to look like a name: letters, not just marks and digits.
refuse.reserved: That name is reserved for the site itself.
refuse.vulgar: This name goes on a public leaderboard. Not this one.
fail.network: No connection to the server. Nothing was created — your name is fine, try again in a moment.
fail.serverDown: The service is not reachable right now (error {status}). This is not about your name — try again in a few minutes.
fail.nameRefused: The name was refused. Pick another one.
fail.unexpected: Unexpected answer from the server (error {status}). This is not about your name.
fail.unknown: The account could not be created. This is not about your name — try again.
status.heading: Where you stand
status.unavailable: The figures are not available right now. What is played is played — it is in the record, not in this browser. {START_TAG_BUTTON}Reload{CLOSE_TAG_BUTTON}
status.locked.why: {START_TAG_STRONG}{INTERPOLATION}{CLOSE_TAG_STRONG} more {ICU}, then the statistics unlock. Before that a hit rate says nothing: over so few attempts, pure guessing regularly looks like a gift.
status.locked.abandoned: {START_TAG_STRONG}{INTERPOLATION}{CLOSE_TAG_STRONG} {ICU} abandoned — that is in the record too, from the first one on.
status.detail.note: The deviation is the more striking figure, the assured minimum the sturdier one: it weighs in how often you have played. Both stand over {START_TAG_STRONG}{INTERPOLATION}{CLOSE_TAG_STRONG} scored sessions with {START_TAG_STRONG}{INTERPOLATION_1}{CLOSE_TAG_STRONG} hits, and they only move at the next block boundary — otherwise you could stop as soon as the number flattered you.
meter.you.label: You
board.eyebrow: Leaderboard · sorted by assured minimum rate
board.heading: Who stands above the baseline
board.lede: Ranks are shares, not places — Annunaki are always the top 0.1 %, however many are playing. Sorting is by the assured minimum rate, because it weighs in the number of sessions. The deviation stands beside it: the more striking but weaker figure. {START_LINK}The whole ladder{CLOSE_LINK} is on the statistics page, next to the distribution it comes from.
board.unavailable: The leaderboard is not available right now.
board.nextBand: eligible players. {START_TAG_STRONG}{INTERPOLATION}{CLOSE_TAG_STRONG} exists from {INTERPOLATION_1} on — with a small field a top place would be no finding, just the best throw of a small round.
board.allBands: eligible players. Every band is filled.
board.empty: Nobody on the list yet. Eligible from {INTERPOLATION} sessions across at least {INTERPOLATION_1} different days — and no row here is invented, so it stays empty until somebody gets there.
board.col.name: Name
board.maskedTitle: Name not approved yet — the id beside it stays verifiable
board.note: Eligible from {INTERPOLATION} sessions across at least {INTERPOLATION_1} different days. Across several days, because running them in parallel does not compress a calendar — and because spread-out sessions are the better data anyway.
board.recomputed: Ranks last recomputed {INTERPOLATION}; they follow along roughly every fifteen minutes.

legal.about.p: vriltrainer is a public forced-choice experiment in remote viewing. The expected hit rate is 12.5 % — pure guessing. Ranks, titles and illustrations are satire on the relevant mythology and are not a claim about reality.

stats.noTrialsYet: No completed session yet. Until there is one, no rate stands here — {START_TAG_STRONG}an invented one would be the only dishonest figure on this page.{CLOSE_TAG_STRONG}
stats.tails.noteEmpty: This is where the players more than {INTERPOLATION} σ above and below chance will stand. Under pure chance there are roughly as many at each end — that is the whole test, and it needs no statistics, only a look.
stats.verdict.notable: that is notable — and not yet an explanation.
stats.tails.headWithBounds: The two ends · accounts from {INTERPOLATION} sessions, {INTERPOLATION_1} σ
stats.tails.note: Under pure chance both ends weigh roughly the same. A real ability could only make the upper one heavier — as long as the two figures resemble each other, what is on screen is what was to be expected.
stats.unavailable.head: Figures not available
stats.unavailable.lead: The overall figures come from the server and are not invented here — so nothing stands here while it is not answering. {START_TAG_BUTTON}Try again{CLOSE_TAG_BUTTON}
stats.mine.noAccount: No account yet. Starting a session creates one — after that your own standing appears here beside everybody else's.
stats.mine.unavailable: Your figures are not available right now.
stats.mine.locked: Unlocked after {INTERPOLATION} sessions — {START_TAG_STRONG}{INTERPOLATION_1}{CLOSE_TAG_STRONG} to go. A hit rate out of {INTERPOLATION_2} attempts would be no finding, it would be an anecdote.
stats.mine.abandoned: Abandoned: {START_TAG_STRONG}{INTERPOLATION}{CLOSE_TAG_STRONG} — counted in from the start.
stats.mine.basis: Deviation and assured minimum stand over {INTERPOLATION} scored sessions with {INTERPOLATION_1} hits. Sessions and rate above are the running total — so the two figures are allowed to disagree about the {START_EMPHASISED_TEXT}n{CLOSE_EMPHASISED_TEXT}, and both are right.
read.baseline.d: One target out of eight. Anyone guessing hits every eighth time on average. Every figure on this page is a deviation from that line, not from zero.
read.falsePositives.t: False positives are the rule here, not the exception
read.falsePositives.d: Let enough people roll dice and you always get somebody with an astonishing streak — that is a statement about the number of people, not about the person. Which is why both ends stand side by side above, and not only the upper one.
read.symmetry.t: Both ends equally heavy means: no effect
read.symmetry.d: A real ability could only make the upper end heavier. As long as the two figures resemble each other, what is on screen is what was to be expected. That needs no statistics, only a look at the symmetry.
read.ranks.t: Ranks are shares, not top places
read.ranks.d: Annunaki are the top 0.1 %, Loosh Farmers the top 0.5 %, and so on — mirrored downwards. A share means the same whether nine people play or nine hundred thousand; a third place does not. A band is only awarded once the share arithmetically covers at least one person — which is why each rank says from what field size it exists.
read.multiAccounts.t: Multiple accounts are priced in, not fought
read.multiAccounts.d: Anyone who creates twenty accounts and shows off the best one is doing exactly what the figures above already measure: many attempts, one of which looks good. No scoring rule repairs that, so none is claimed — the overall rate and the two ends remain the finding, not the topmost row.
read.wilson.t: The assured minimum beats the deviation
read.wilson.d: The deviation in σ is the more striking figure, the assured minimum rate the sturdier one: it weighs in how often somebody has played. Three hits out of eight are not a gift, they are a Tuesday afternoon.
read.yours.d: Of 10,000 people with no ability whatsoever, {START_TAG_SPAN}{INTERPOLATION}{CLOSE_TAG_SPAN} reach this figure on luck alone. Without this line the number cannot be interpreted.
trial.starting: The server fixes the target and writes it into the record before it answers.
trial.sealed.note: The target is sealed with this number {START_EMPHASISED_TEXT}before{CLOSE_EMPHASISED_TEXT} you choose. After the reveal you recompute all of this yourself — completely, byte by byte.
trial.takeYourTime: Take your time with the coordinate. Only then reveal.
trial.answering: The choice is on its way. It is scored only once the server has written it into the record.
trial.tooFast: Too fast! At least three seconds between reveal and choice. The answer was not looked at, the session is still running.
proof.title: Proof
proof.eyebrow: The full derivation, computed in your browser
proof.h.pool: Which pool it is computed against
proof.pool.lead: The derivation draws against {START_EMPHASISED_TEXT}indices{CLOSE_EMPHASISED_TEXT} in the manifest. A different manifest yields different images from the same seed — which is why it is rehashed here and compared with the hash that already came with the coordinate.
proof.hashed.lead: Every field is length-prefixed so the boundaries are unambiguous: {START_TAG_CODE}framed(p₀, p₁, …) = SHA-256( LE64(|p₀|) ‖ p₀ ‖ LE64(|p₁|) ‖ p₁ ‖ … ){CLOSE_TAG_CODE} Without it, {START_TAG_CODE}("ab","c"){CLOSE_TAG_CODE} and {START_TAG_CODE}("a","bc"){CLOSE_TAG_CODE} hash alike.
proof.preimage.commitment: The full preimage string, {INTERPOLATION} bytes — exactly these bytes go into SHA-256:
proof.matches: Identical. The target was fixed before you chose.
proof.mismatch: Does not match. That would be a reason not to believe this site.
proof.h.seed: How the seed became the eight images
proof.keystream: The seed produces the keystream {START_TAG_CODE}block(i) = SHA-256( seed ‖ LE64(i) ){CLOSE_TAG_CODE}, read as 64-bit words little-endian. From it, in this order:
proof.independence: Computed with an implementation written independently of the server's. Both are checked against the same test vectors — that is the point: a check using the server's own code checks nothing. The computation runs in the browser; an independent third-party verifier does not exist in this version yet.
proof.manifestFailed: The pool manifest for this session could not be loaded. Without the list of images in exactly the published order there is nothing to recompute — and an empty proof panel would look like a test that passed.
proof.manifest.rehash: The recomputed hash of the manifest differs from the one it names itself.
proof.manifest.mismatch: The manifest delivered is not the one this session was fixed against.
proof.check.seal.ok: The values now disclosed produce exactly the number that stood on screen before your choice.
proof.check.seal.bad: The number from before cannot be reproduced from the disclosed values.
proof.check.echo.ok: The 32 bytes from your browser come back unchanged — the seed has two sides.
proof.check.echo.bad: The server returns different 32 bytes than your browser sent.
proof.check.draw.ok: The seed produces exactly these eight images, in exactly this order.
proof.check.draw.bad: The seed produces a different selection or a different order than the one shown.
proof.check.target.none: Without a derivation there is no recomputed target.
proof.check.target.ok: The recomputed target is the same one your choice was scored against.
proof.check.target.bad: The recomputed target is a different one from the one scored.
proof.note.echoed: 32 bytes from your browser, returned unchanged by the server
proof.note.overSorted: Over the sorted (id, category) pairs, categories first
proof.note.uniform: Uniform over the eight, independent of category size
